title: Add spectral deconfounder detector and thermostat rollback guard
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context and motivation: Continuous canary detectors at Redwood are effective for gross regressions but still struggle when covariate drift and correlated traffic noise create false positives. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) a spectral deconfounder detector that separates persistent signal drift from high-frequency noise and correlated load artifacts, and (2) a thermostat rollback guard that enforces a time- and severity-aware rollback budget (a.k.a. "thermostat") to avoid oscillatory rollback/redeploy cycles during transient perturbations.

Summary of changes: added a new detector implementation (spectral_deconfounder) which performs short-window spectral decomposition and robust trend estimation on latency and throughput time series; extended the canary orchestrator to accept detector confidence scores and incorporate a drift-adjusted threshold; implemented the thermostat rollback guard that encodes cooldown windows, graduated rollback severity, and escalation gating. The thermostat also exposes a soft-fail mode for canaries that notifies but does not immediately rollback, useful for gradually ramped cutovers.

Why this is different: unlike simple percentile or EWMA detectors, spectral deconfounder explicitly models periodic and multi-frequency components and performs robust low-rank trend extraction before making alarm decisions; this reduces false positives during coordinated traffic shifts (e.g., multi-region bursts) while preserving sensitivity to genuine latency inflation. The thermostat guard provides a principled policy for rollback inertia and budgeted rollback credits derived from historical canary stability.

Implementation notes: the detector is implemented in perf-canary/detectors/spectral_deconfounder.go and relies on a lightweight FFT and robust median filtering (no external native deps). The orchestrator changes are in perf-canary/orchestrator/controller.py and include a new signals API to accept detector confidence and spectral-variance metadata. The thermostat guard lives under perf-canary/guards/thermostat_guard.py and is configurable via canary policy YAML (observability/canary_policies/thermostat-default.yml).

Testing and validation: local unit tests added for decomposition edge cases and confidence scoring (tests/perf_canary/test_spectral_deconfounder.py). A simulated traffic harness (tools/canary-simulator) was extended to replay historical bursts and run 5k simulated canary experiments. On the 12-day replay we observed: reduction in alerting false positives from 18% -> 10% (relative -44%), median time-to-detect genuine regressions preserved (within 0-2s of baseline), and rollback oscillations reduced by ~60% when thermostat was enabled.

Rollout plan: merge to main, dogfood on perf-canary staging for 48h with thermostat in soft-fail mode, then enable active rollback on a small set of low-risk experiments (5% traffic) for 24h. If metric drift stabilizes for 72h we will expand to default canaries. Canary rollout policy includes a conservative backoff: thermostat triggers automatic rollback only when either (A) detector confidence > 0.9 and sustained delta > 15% for 10m, or (B) 3 contiguous sliding windows each exceed severity thresholds and budget permits.

Operational notes: new telemetry emitted: perf.canary.spectral.variance, perf.canary.deconfounder.confidence, perf.canary.thermostat.credit_balance. Grafana dashboard panel added in observability/dashboards/canary_spectral_overview.json. Alerting changes: alert perf-canary-thermostat-credit-low (warn when credit balance below 20% of historical median).

Dependencies and compatibility: no breaking API changes. All new flags default to off for existing canaries. Config keys documented in observability/canary_policies/README.md.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests (simulator) extended
- [x] Dashboard + alerts updated
- [x] Linear tickets linked
- [x] Rollout plan documented

Notes for reviewers: focus on the confidence scoring math and the thermostat credit accounting code paths. The spectral decomposition uses a tunable window length (default 120s) and an L1 median filter to avoid contamination from large outliers.

Related work: complements the existing percentile- and probe-based detectors; intended to be composable with ensemble detectors in perf-canary/orchestrator.

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main after reviewer approvals and a CI rerun of the flaky integration test.

a91c3e7: expose detector confidence in orchestrator signals API
b6e2f11: implement thermostat rollback guard and credit accounting
c3a91f4: add canary simulator scenarios for spectral noise and integration tests
e5b0d2a: add dashboard panels and alert rule for thermostat credit low
review_comments: Luis Moreno (reviewer): The noise floor estimation looks good but please add a short-circuit for extremely sparse traffic windows ( < 10 samples ) to avoid NaNs.
Maya Chen (author): Good catch — added a guard and included unit tests for sparse windows (see test_spectral_deconfounder.py).
Sofia Gupta (reviewer): Please make thermostat credit config cluster-scoped instead of per-canary by default; also document the credits calculation clearly.
Maya Chen (author): Changed default to cluster-scoped and added section in README.md explaining credit derivation and decay schedule.
Evan Brooks (approver): Ran simulator locally; numbers look reasonable. Approve after CI rerun for flaky "canary-simulator" test.
release_notes: Adds spectral deconfounder detector to reduce false-positive canary alerts during correlated traffic noise and a thermostat rollback guard to stabilize rollback behavior; telemetry and dashboards included. Rollout in soft-fail mode recommended before enabling automatic rollback.
